newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-RESURGENT BECKER BACK TO HIS BEST IN STUTTGART FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RESURGENT BECKER BACK TO HIS BEST IN STUTTGART FINAL.

text.p: Boris Becker proved on Sunday that he is back to his impressive best after a serious wrist injury when he defeated world number one Pete Sampras in the Stuttgart Open final.
Becker delighted his fanatical home fans by coming back twice from behind to end Sampras's 21-match unbeaten run. He won 3-6 6-3 3-6 6-3 6-4.
Samras had been seeking his fourth consecutive tournament victory, including the U.S. Open.
But he was thwarted by a resurgent Becker who had played some superb tennis on his way to the final, including a semifinal victory over world number two Michael Chang.
Becker surprised even himself with the performance in the final which lasted just under three hours.
"I am a bit perplexed. I never expected to be able to beat him," Becker said. "But you try everything against Pete Sampras in a final like this. My legs hurt in the final set."
Becker is now almost certain to qualify for next month's season-ending world championship in Hanover.
